paras: The killing of Henry Herndon was the fatal shooting of a Black man, described as "colored," by James Dameron, a policeman, at Springfield, Missouri, in late 1882. It is known only from a one-line item in a Kentucky paper's news column, which attributed the shooting to "an old grudge."

According to the Maysville Evening Bulletin, Dameron "shot and killed Henry Herndon, colored" at Springfield. The item gave no date, place within the town, or account of the encounter, and named the cause only as "An old grudge." Other items in the same column described Christmas Day and Christmas night violence elsewhere, but the shooting itself was not dated.
The brief did not say whether Dameron was arrested, and no report of an inquest, charge or trial appears in the coverage.

The Evening Bulletin of Maysville, Kentucky, ran the item on December 29, 1882, in its "News Brevities" column, between a dismissal at a Xenia, Ohio, orphans' home and a coal operators' wage cut at Massillon, Ohio. The paper identified Herndon by race and Dameron by occupation, offered a personal grudge as the motive, and made no comment on a policeman killing a man. No other paper's account of the shooting, Missouri or otherwise, appears in the coverage.
